sections.h2: What kind of county is Ross County, Ohio, for a home seller?
sections.html:
Ross County is a large, hilly, mostly rural county in Appalachian Ohio, and Chillicothe is both the county seat and the only city. Organized on August 20, 1798 as the sixth county of the Northwest Territory, it is the second largest Ohio county by land area, behind only Ashtabula. The Scioto River runs south through the east-central part of the county and Paint Creek joins it southeast of Chillicothe.

Outside Chillicothe the county has villages such as Adelphi, Bainbridge, Clarksburg, Frankfort, Kingston and South Salem, and 16 townships. Eleven school districts reach into the county, among them Chillicothe City, Huntington Local, Paint Valley Local, Southeastern Local, Zane Trace Local, Adena Local and Waverly City. Ohio University runs a regional campus in Chillicothe.

The Census Bureau counts 76,429 residents for July 1, 2025 and 32,165 housing units. Owners occupy 69.6% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $171,500, median gross rent is $906 and median household income is $61,303. Mean travel time to work is 26.4 minutes, against 21.8 in Richland County, which fits a county of 689 square miles with about 112 people per square mile.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Ross County?
sections.html:
The county auditor values property and the county treasurer bills and collects. The treasurer's office is in the Ross County Courthouse at 2 North Paint Street, Suite F, Chillicothe, Ohio 45601, and the phone is 740-702-3080, the same number the treasurer's pages give for auditor questions. The email for the treasurer is treasurer@rosscountyohio.gov. The auditor runs an online parcel search and a tax estimator on its own site.

The Board of Revision has three members: the treasurer, the auditor and the president of the board of county commissioners. Valuation complaints go to the auditor's office, which presents them to the Board.

Ross County bills reflect values set a year earlier. The treasurer's site notes that real estate taxes are collected one year in arrears, so taxes paid in 2026 cover the 2025 obligation. Auditors reassess at least every six years, with a triennial update at the halfway point.

sections.h2: When are Ross County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
The treasurer's collection page lists first-half 2026 payments due February 20 and second-half payments due August 21, with a rule that a due date falling on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Both of those dates have passed. Bills for the next cycle go out in mid-January and again in mid-June or early July, so ask the treasurer for the exact 2027 dates. State law, in section 323.12 of the Revised Code, sets December 31 and June 20 as the base dates unless a county extends them.

The treasurer's FAQ spells out the penalty rules, and the table below pulls the main ones together.

Ross County Treasurer and Auditor rules on penalties and deadlines
ItemRule
Late payment received within 10 calendar days5% penalty
Any later payment10% penalty
Prior-year taxes carried overInterest charged August 1
All past-due taxesInterest charged December 1
Delinquent list publicationPay or sign a contract by October 31 to stay off the auditor's list
Owner occupancy applicationJanuary 1 to the first Monday in June
Valuation complaintJanuary 1 to March 31

Source: Ross County Treasurer FAQ and Reducing Your Taxes pages.

For mailed payments, the treasurer follows the postmark rule in state law and warns that a postmark often reflects the date the piece was first processed, not the date it was dropped off. Mail early. A personal check is accepted, but the treasurer will take only cash, a cashier's check or a money order from anyone whose earlier payment failed to clear.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Ross County homeowners apply for?
sections.html:
The owner occupancy credit takes a reduction off the home site and the house for owners who live there as a principal residence. Apply with the County Auditor between January 1 and the first Monday in June. It does not apply to rentals, corporate or partnership owners, units in retail or commercial buildings, depreciation-taxed manufactured homes, or acreage beyond one acre.

The homestead exemption is run through the same office. The Ohio Department of Taxation lists the reduction for a low-income senior or disabled owner at $29,700 of home value for tax year 2026 real property, with an income threshold of $41,000 for that year. A disabled veteran or the surviving spouse of a public service officer killed in the line of duty gets a reduction of $59,400 and faces no income test. The credit equals the tax charged on that slice of value, so a higher local rate means a larger credit. Applications for real property are due by December 31 of the year they apply to.

  • Penalty remission: request it from the treasurer on Form 23A, and only for reasons Ohio law allows.
  • Military extension: National Guard and reserve members called to active duty, or a spouse or dependent parent applying for them, can get up to five years to pay without penalty or interest.
  • Monthly Budget Pay Plan: a free service that lets owners pay a little each month toward the next bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Ross County property valuation?
sections.html:
Owners who disagree with the auditor's value can file a complaint with the Board of Revision through the auditor's office between January 1 and March 31. Under section 5715.19 the statutory deadline is March 31 or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later, and a mailed complaint counts on its postmark date. The hearing notice must go out at least ten days ahead, and the board has 180 days after the filing deadline to decide.

The treasurer's page tells owners the strongest evidence is usually the recent sale price shown by closing papers. If the house has not sold lately, bring the sale prices of comparable homes. Photographs that show the condition of the property can help. Section 5715.19 also bars a second complaint on the same parcel within the same interim period unless the property sold at arm's length, lost value to casualty, gained a substantial improvement, or saw occupancy change by at least 15 percent.

While a complaint is pending, the owner may tender taxes computed on the value claimed in the complaint, and the treasurer must accept that tender.

sections.h2: What are Ross County's options for delinquent taxes?
sections.html:
The treasurer offers two plans meant to keep owners out of foreclosure. A Delinquent Tax Contract splits back taxes into five equal installments, with the first due at signing and the rest added to the next four February and July bills. A SMART Payments plan folds current taxes and past-due taxes into one monthly payment that can run 30 months or longer. Under both, no new interest or penalty is added once the contract is signed and the first payment is made, but missing a payment cancels the contract and the stopped charges return. If legal action has already begun, a court cost is added to the first payment.

The treasurer's FAQ says the auditor publishes the delinquent tax list and recommends paying or signing a contract by October 31 to avoid publication. It also says there is no fixed date by which a property is foreclosed, and that the office will work with owners who are struggling.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 and 2026 state reforms change in Ross County?
sections.html: The treasurer's site summarizes five property tax bills signed in late 2025 and early 2026. One changes how sales ratio studies pick the sales used in valuation. One revises the 20-mill floor calculation. One creates an inflation cap credit for school districts at the floor, and the treasurer states that all of the county's school districts sit at the 20-mill floor, with the credit showing up only in the second-half 2026 collection. One lets county budget commissions trim levies judged unnecessarily high. One caps growth in inside millage at the rate of inflation during reappraisals and triennial updates.

sections.h2: How do I handle property tax when selling in Ross County?
sections.html:
Taxes sit on the property and not on the owner, so a buyer can receive a bill after closing. The treasurer notes that a credit for prorated taxes is typically given to the purchaser in the closing papers, which is why the settlement statement matters. Get the treasurer's balance in writing before you sign, and ask whether a delinquent tax contract is open on the parcel.

Before the deed is recorded, the auditor must endorse it. Under section 319.202, the buyer files a statement of value and answers questions about owner occupancy reductions and CAUV farm status, while the seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax. Section 322.02 lets a county levy that transfer tax at up to thirty cents per hundred dollars, paid to the auditor before the deed goes to the recorder. Ask the Ross County Auditor which rate applies.

faqs.q: When are Ross County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The 2026 collections were due February 20 and August 21. Bills mail in mid-January and mid-June or early July, and a date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Ask the treasurer at 740-702-3080 for the next dates.

faqs.q: What is the Ross County late penalty?
faqs.a: A payment received within ten calendar days after the due date draws 5%, and any later payment draws 10%. Interest on carried-over taxes starts August 1, and December 1 adds interest on all past-due taxes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Ross County valuation?
faqs.a: File with the County Auditor between January 1 and March 31. State law lets the deadline run later if first-half collection closes after March 31.

faqs.q: How do I stay off the Ross County delinquent tax list?
faqs.a: Pay the balance or sign a contract with the treasurer by October 31. The treasurer says the payment must be received, not postmarked, by the auditor's cutoff.

faqs.q: Who records the deed after a Ross County sale?
faqs.a: The Ross County Recorder, at 2 North Paint Street, Suite E in Chillicothe, phone 740-702-3000. The auditor must endorse the deed first.
